name: Ephara's Dispersal
oracle_text:
This spell costs {2} less to cast if it targets an attacking creature.
Return target creature to its owner's hand. Surveil 2. (Look at the top two cards of your library, then put any number of them into your graveyard and the rest on top of your library in any order.)
blocked_sentences: This spell costs {2} less to cast if it targets an attacking creature

needs.what: a card-level `cost_reduction` gated on the spell's OWN chosen targets: `{"amount": 2, "targeting": {"types": ["Creature"], "attacking": true}}` (or a condition head reading the cast's target tuple) so the spell is priced {2} cheaper exactly when one of its declared targets matches the selector. `cost_reduction()` already receives the cast's `targets` (it hands them to `spell_cost_reduction`/`spell_mana_tax`); `reduction_amount(card.cost_reduction)` would need them too, read generously while targets are still None at the legality gate, as the `spell_cost_reduction` targeting clause already is. Same shape as Ranger's Guile-era 'costs {N} less if it targets ...' printings (e.g. Dive Down-style, Sigiled Starfish-free cycle)
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `cost_reduction` takes `amount` + `condition`, but `reduction_amount` is target-blind and the loader narrows `condition` to heads answerable at pricing time (is_monarch, exists, cmp...), none of which reads the spell's targets. `condition: {exists: attacking creature}` would discount the spell whenever any creature is attacking, even when it targets a non-attacker -- strictly better than printed. The `spell_cost_reduction` static's targeting clause reads targets but discounts other spells from a permanent, not the card itself
